workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§237–241
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§237–241: The Forest Peoples and the Tumad
part: §§237–241 — The Forest Peoples and the Tumad
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§237–241, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: The Uighur Idu'ut seeks the Qahan's favour, Jebe having wiped out Küchülüg of the Naiman (§§237–238); Jüchi, in the Year of the Hare, leads the right wing against the Forest People, who submit one after another, and is told by his father to take them as his own (§239). Boroqul is killed by Tumad scouts, and Dorbai the Doqshin avenges him by a ruse (§240); Qorchi and Quduqa Beki are in turn seized by the Tumad, and the section ends with the Qahan's gifts of women and people (§241). Grammar to watch: the long converb chains in -žu/-žü, the ablative and instrumental lists of gifts, the passive in -γda-, and the quotation closed by keġen, where Shiratori prints marks only partly and the notes say where `i` supplies one.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Žebe Naiman-u Küčülüg Qān-i nekežü Sariγ γun-a güjičežü Küčülüg-i muqudγažu irebe.

morph.gloss: Jebe, a man's name (not the common noun žebe 'weapon') [人名]
qan, ruler (short form beside qaγan) [皇帝行]
to pursue (stem inferred from the Ming 追襲) [追襲着]
cliff, crag (stem inferred from the Ming 崖; uncertain) [崖行]
to overtake, catch up (stem inferred from the Ming 趕上) [趕上着]
to wipe out, destroy (Ming 窮絕) [敎窮絕了着]

sentences.l: Žebe, Naiman-of Küčülüg Qān-(object) pursuing, Sariγ cliff-at overtaking, Küčülüg-(object) having-wiped-out, came.
sentences.i: Jebe pursued Küchülüg Qan of the Naiman, overtook him at the cliff of Sariq, wiped Küchülüg out, and came.
sentences.n: Read it as one converb chain ending in irebe 'came' (Ming 來了): nekežü 'pursuing' (-žü, Ming 着), güjičežü 'overtaking', muqudγažu 'wiping out'. Qān-i and Küčülüg-i carry the accusative -i (the Ming writes 行 for it): Küchülüg is the object of the pursuit and again of the killing. Žebe is the man's name here (Ming 人名), not the common noun 'weapon'. Doubtful: γun-a (Ming 崖行 'at the cliff') is read as γun + dative-locative -a, a stem I know only from this Ming gloss; Sariγ is a place name (Ming 地名). muqudγa- has the Ming 窮絕 'cut off, brought to an end', so 'wiped out'.

sentences.t: Uiγ̇ud-un Iduγ̇ud Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur elčin iležüġü.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant)
Idu'ut, a man's name (Ming 人名; later a title of the Uighur rulers) [人名]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to send (Ming 敎來了; the Ming reads 'caused to come') [敎來了]

sentences.l: Uighurs-of Iduγ̇ud, Chinggis Qaγan-to envoy sent.
sentences.i: The Idu'ut of the Uighurs sent an envoy to Chinggis Qahan.
sentences.n: Uiγ̇ud-un is the genitive after a consonant (-un), 'of the Uighurs'; Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur has the dative-locative -dur (Ming 行), 'to Chinggis Qahan'. iležüġü is ile- 'to send' with the narrative past -žüġü. Doubtful: the Ming glosses it 敎來了 'caused to come', which would make the envoy the thing sent, as I have it; the next unit makes the envoys two men, so I keep 'sent an envoy' as a collective singular. Iduγ̇ud is a man's name in the Ming (人名); I leave it as 'Idu'ut', which is the form later readers know as a title of the Uighur rulers, but nothing in this text says so.

sentences.t: Adkiraγ, Darbai qojar elčin(i)-jer öčižü irerün:

morph.gloss: two (follows the pair it counts) [兩箇]
to report, speak to a superior (stem inferred from the Ming 奏) [奏着]

sentences.l: Adkiraγ, Darbai two envoy(i)-with reporting, coming-when:
sentences.i: Adkiraq and Darbai, the two of them, came as envoys and said:
sentences.n: qojar 'two' follows the pair it counts (Ming 兩箇). elčin(i)-jer is elčin 'envoy' plus the instrumental -jer with Shiratori's linking (i); the Ming 使臣敎 reads 'as envoys, causing'. öčižü is a converb in -žü (Ming 奏着 'reporting to a superior'); the stem öči- is inferred from that Ming. irerün is ire- 'to come' with the converb of time -rün, 'when coming'. Doubtful: whether 'with envoys' means they were themselves the envoys or sent through envoys; I take the first. Shiratori's colon leads into the speech, which opens with a quotation mark on the next word.

sentences.t: "Eġülen arilžu eke naran üžegsen metü mölsün arilžu müren usun oluγsan metü

morph.gloss: to clear, become clear (stem inferred from the Ming 淨) [淨着]
mother (the Ming 母; here before naran, 'the sun, the mother'? uncertain) [母]
to see, be shown (Ming 見) [見了]
to clear, become clear (stem inferred from the Ming 淨) [淨着]

sentences.l: "Cloud clearing, mother sun seen like, ice clearing, river water got like,
sentences.i: “Like seeing the sun as the clouds clear, like finding river water as the ice clears,
sentences.n: Two similes of the same shape: a converb in -žu (arilžu, Ming 淨着 'clearing, becoming clear') and a past participle (üžegsen 'seen', oluγsan 'got'), then metü 'like' (Ming 般). So 'the clouds clearing, [like] the sun seen' and 'the ice clearing, [like] river water got'. Doubtful: eke naran, Ming 母 日 'mother sun': eke 'mother' may be an epithet of the sun or a first member of a compound; I keep it as 'mother sun' in the literal and drop it in the plain line. müren usun 'river water' (Ming 河 水) is read as the object of oluγsan 'got, found'. aril- is inferred from the Ming 淨. The opening mark on Eġülen is Shiratori's; the speech closes at ögsü" in a later unit.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-u nere aldar sonosču maši bajasba.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan-of name, fame hearing, greatly rejoiced.
sentences.i: so, hearing the name and fame of Chinggis Qahan, he rejoiced greatly.
sentences.n: Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-u is the genitive -u (the form after n), 'of Chinggis Qahan', before nere aldar 'name, fame' (Ming 名 聲). sonosču is a converb in -ču (Ming 聽着) and bajasba the past in -ba (Ming 喜歡了). The envoys are speaking about the Idu'ut, so the 'he' is supplied: the verb has no subject marker. The 'so' in the plain line carries the force of the two similes before it.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan sojurγaγ̇asu altan büse-jin γorgid-ača al deġel-ün hürtesün-eče oluγ̇asu

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

words.reading: 莎余舌兒中合阿速 sojurγaγ̇asu

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow a grace (Ming 恩賜) [恩賜呵]
ring, loop, buckle (Ming 彄兒; sense uncertain) [彄兒 每行]
scrap, snip of cut cloth (Ming 碎裁帛) [碎裁帛行]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan favouring-if, gold belt-of rings-from, red garment-of scraps-from getting-if,
sentences.i: If Chinggis Qahan will show favour, if I may get a ring from a gold belt, a scrap of red cloth,
sentences.n: Two conditionals: sojurγaγ̇asu (-γ̇asu, Ming 呵 'if, when') and oluγ̇asu (Ming 得呵). The things hoped for are named with the ablative: γorgid-ača (-ača, Ming 行 'from') and hürtesün-eče (-eče, Ming 行 here too). Doubtful: γorgid is read as the plural of a word 'ring, buckle' from the Ming 彄兒 and büse-jin 'of the belt' (-jin after a vowel); hürtesün is 'scrap of cut cloth' from the Ming 碎裁帛. The sense 'the least favour, a ring from a belt, a scrap of a coat' is the Ming's, and I have kept the grammar of 'from' in the literal and softened it in the plain line. al (Ming 大紅) is 'red'.

sentences.t: dabtuγ̇ar köġün čin-u bolžu küčü ögsü" keġen öčižü irežüġüi.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (back-vowel form) (on the oblique stem: 'your')
optative: let it be given, I will give
to report, speak to a superior (stem inferred from the Ming 奏) [奏着]

sentences.l: fifth son your becoming, strength I will give" saying, reporting came.
sentences.i: I shall become your fifth son and give you my strength,” they said, reporting it, and came.
sentences.n: dabtuγ̇ar köġün čin-u bolžu is 'becoming your fifth son': čin-u is či 'you' in the oblique stem čin- with the genitive -u (Ming 你的). küčü ögsü is 'strength I will give': ögsü is ög- 'to give' with the optative -sü (Ming 與). The closing mark on ögsü" is Shiratori's. keġen 'saying' is the converb that closes a quotation, then öčižü and irežüġüi (the front-vowel narrative past, Ming 來了). Doubtful: 'fifth son' is the Ming's 第五 子; the four sons of Chinggis already named make the Idu'ut the fifth. The subject of keġen öčižü irežüġüi is the two envoys of §238 (U2): the whole speech from Eġülen on is their report, in which the Idu'ut speaks of himself as 'I'.

sentences.t: Tere üge-dür Čiṅgis Qaγan sojurγažu qariγ̇u ügüležü ilerün;

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]
to show favour, bestow grace [恩賜着]

sentences.l: That word-in Chinggis Qaγan favouring, answer speaking sending-when;
sentences.i: At those words Chinggis Qahan showed his favour, and when he sent back an answer, he said:
sentences.n: tere üge-dür is 'in that word' (Ming 那 言語裏), with the front-vowel dative-locative -dür. sojurγažu and ügüležü are converbs (-žu, -žü; Ming 恩賜着, 話); qariγ̇u 'answer' (Ming 囘). ilerün is ile- 'to send' with the converb of time -rün; the Ming gives 去 'go', so 'when sending' is the literal reading and 'when sending (them) back' in the plain line is a fair rendering, though 'going' is another possible reading. The semicolon is Shiratori's; the speech opens at the next word.

sentences.t: "Öki ber öġüje; dabtuγ̇ar köġün boltuγai.
sentences.l: "Daughter too I will give; fifth son let be.
sentences.i: “I shall give my daughter too, and he shall be my fifth son.
sentences.n: öki 'girl, daughter' plus ber 'also' (Ming 也); öġüje 'let us give' (hortative -üje, Ming 咱 'we'). Doubtful: the Ming reads the hortative as 'we', but I read a speaker's own offer, 'I will give'. boltuγai is the third-person optative (bol- 'to become', Ming 做者 'let it be'): the Idu'ut is to be fifth son. The opening mark on "Öki is Shiratori's; the speech closes at iretügei".

sentences.l: Gold, silver, pearls, large-pearls, gold-brocades, whole-gold-brocades, bolts-of-silk taking Iduγ̇ud let-come" saying, if-he-send.
sentences.i: Let the Idu'ut come bringing gold, silver, pearls, big pearls, gold brocades, cloth of gold and bolts of silk,” he said, and sent word.
sentences.n: A list of gifts, each with the plural: subud, tanas, načid, dardas, torγad (-d, -s, Ming 每). The stems are inferred from the Ming and are uncertain: 'pearl', 'big pearl' (Ming 珠, 大珠), 'gold brocade' (金段子), 'whole-gold brocade' (渾金段子), 'bolt of silk' (段匹). abuγ̇ad is ab- 'to take' with the converb of completion (Ming 將來了 'bringing'). iretügei is the third-person optative (-tügei, Ming 者), 'let him come'. keġežü ilebesü: 'saying, if (he) sends'; ilebesü is a conditional in -besü (Ming 去呵), here carrying the sense 'when he sent (word)'. The closing mark on iretügei" is Shiratori's.

words.reading: 莎余(舌兒)中合黑荅罷 sojurγaγdaba

sentences.l: Iduγ̇ud was-favoured saying, rejoicing, gold, silver, pearls, large-pearls, bolts-of-silk, gold-brocades, whole-gold-brocades, lengths-of-cloth taking,
sentences.i: The Idu'ut was delighted at being favoured. He took gold, silver, pearls, big pearls, bolts of silk, gold brocades, cloth of gold and lengths of cloth,
sentences.n: sojurγaγdaba is the passive of sojurγa- 'to show favour' (-γda-, Ming 被恩賜了 'was favoured'). keġen closes the thought ('so saying'), then bajasču 'rejoicing' (converb in -ču, Ming 喜歡了着). The list repeats the gifts of the Qahan's message with the plurals -d, -s; aγ̇urasun (Ming (段)子) is a further item, 'lengths of cloth' (the stem is as printed; uncertain). The chain continues to abuγ̇ad, 'taking'.

sentences.t: Iduγ̇ud irežü Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur aγ̇ulžaba.

morph.gloss: Idu'ut, a man's name (Ming 人名; later a title of the Uighur rulers) [人名]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to have an audience, present oneself and pay respects (Ming 拜見) [拜見了]

sentences.l: Iduγ̇ud coming, Chinggis Qaγan-to had-an-audience.
sentences.i: The Idu'ut came and paid his respects to Chinggis Qahan.
sentences.n: irežü 'coming' (Ming 來着), aγ̇ulžaba 'had an audience' (Ming 拜見了, a verb I take as aγ̇ulža- 'to have an audience, to present oneself and pay respects'). Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur has the dative-locative -dur, 'before Chinggis Qahan'.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Iduγ̇ud-i sojurγažu Al-Altun-i ögbe.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Idu'ut, a man's name [人名 行]
to show favour, bestow grace [恩賜着]
Al-Altun, a woman's name (al 'red' + altun 'gold') [女子名 行]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan Iduγ̇ud-(object) favouring, Al-Altun-(object) gave.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan showed favour to the Idu'ut and gave him Al-Altun.
sentences.n: Both objects take -i: Iduγ̇ud-i (Ming 人名行) and Al-Altun-i (女子名行). Doubtful: with ögbe 'gave', the Ming's 行 on the first name marks the person favoured, and the second name is the woman given; so 'gave Al-Altun (to him)'. The Mongol does not repeat 'to him'. Al-Altun is a woman's name made from al 'red' and altun 'gold'.

sentences.t: Taγ̇ulai žil Žüči-ji baraγ̇un γar-un čeriġüd(i)-jer hoi-jin irgen-dür morilaγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: Jüchi, a son's name [人名 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant)

words.reading: 扯舌里兀的-耶舌兒 čeriġüd(i)-jer

morph.gloss: people, the common folk [百姓 行]

sentences.l: Hare year Jüči-(object) right hand-of troops-with, forest-of people-to made-to-ride.
sentences.i: In the Year of the Hare he sent Jüchi, with the troops of the right wing, to the Forest People.
sentences.n: Taγ̇ulai žil is 'hare year' (Ming 兎兒年), the Hare year of the twelve-year cycle (the text gives no date in our reckoning). Žüči-ji takes the accusative -ji after a vowel (Ming 行); the verb morilaγ̇ulba is mori 'horse' + the verb-maker -la- 'to ride' + the causative -γ̇ul- + the past -ba (Ming 敎上馬了 'made mount'). baraγ̇un γar-un 'of the right hand' is the right wing of the army. čeriġüd(i)-jer is čerig 'army' + the plural -ġüd + the instrumental -(i)jer, 'with the troops'. hoi-jin irgen-dür is 'to the forest people', with the genitive -jin after a vowel and the dative -dür. Doubtful: -la- is shown here as a verb-maker 'to ride'; in morilan (§240) the same stem is given as mori-.

sentences.t: Buqa γažarčilažu odba.

morph.gloss: Buqa, a man's name (not buqa 'bull') [人名]

words.reading: 中合札舌兒赤剌周 γažarčilažu

sentences.l: Buqa guiding went.
sentences.i: Buqa went as guide.
sentences.n: Buqa is the man's name (Ming 人名), not buqa 'bull'. γažarčilažu is γažar 'land' + -či 'one who' + -la- 'to act as' + the converb -žu: 'acting as guide' (Ming 引路着, 'leading the way'). odba is od- 'to go' with the past -ba.

sentences.t: Oirad-un Quduqa-Beki tümen Oirad-un urida elsen orožu irebe.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant)
Quduqa Beki, a man's name [人名]
genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant)
to submit (stem inferred from the Ming 投降/歸附) [投降]

sentences.l: Oirat-of Quduqa-Beki, ten-thousand Oirat-of, formerly submitting entering, came.
sentences.i: Quduqa Beki of the Oirat, who had earlier submitted, came with ten thousand Oirat.
sentences.n: Oirad-un is the genitive after a consonant (Ming 種名的). tümen is the numeral 'ten thousand' (Ming 萬), as in a unit of that size; it stands after Quduqa-Beki and before Oirad-un, so 'Quduqa Beki's ten thousand of the Oirat'. urida 'formerly' (Ming 先前), elsen 'submitting' (else- inferred from the Ming 投降, with the converb -n) and orožu 'entering' (Ming 入着) make the chain 'having earlier entered in submission'. Doubtful: the order of tümen and the second Oirad-un; I take both as one phrase. 'With' in the plain line is supplied: the Mongol has no instrumental on tümen Oirad-un; the sense is supported by uduridun 'leading' in the parallel clause later in this section.

sentences.t: Irežü Žüči-ji uduridču tümen Oirad-tur(i)-jan γažarčilažu Šiγšid-tur oroγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: Jüchi, a son's name [人名 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
converb: …ing (a form of -žu; the d is unexplained)

words.reading: 斡亦舌剌惕-都︀舌里-顏 Oirad-tur(i)-jan

morph.gloss: the Oirat, a people [種(名) 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (back-vowel form; the (i) before it is Shiratori's)

words.reading: 中合札舌兒赤剌周 γažarčilažu

sentences.l: Coming, Jüči-(object) leading, ten-thousand Oirat-to-own guiding, Šiγšid-to caused-to-enter.
sentences.i: He came, led Jüchi, and guiding his own ten thousand Oirat, brought him into Shiqshid.
sentences.n: Another chain: irežü, uduridču (Ming 引着, 'leading'; -dču is a form of -žu with an unexplained d), γažarčilažu (as above), then oroγ̇ulba 'made enter' (oro- + the causative -γ̇ul- + -ba, Ming 敎入了). Oirad-tur(i)-jan has the dative -tur, Shiratori's linking (i), and the reflexive-possessive -jan 'one's own'; the Ming 種(名) 自的行 'to one's own Oirat'. Doubtful: the subject. The Ming has no subject word; I take Quduqa Beki as the subject (he came and led), and Jüchi as the object of 'leading' and 'brought in', which the accusative -ji of the earlier unit supports. Šiγšid-tur is a place name with -tur (Ming 地名行). The plain line takes 'his own ten thousand Oirat' as those he guided; the dative -tur on Oirad-tur(i)-jan is not shown there.

sentences.t: Žüči Oirad, Burijad, Barγun, Ursud, Qabqanas, Qaṅγas, Tubas-i oroγ̇uluγ̇ad tümen Kirgisud-tur kürüġesü

morph.gloss: the Qangqas, a people (the Ming 破開的 'split open' is not applied) [種(名)]

words.reading: 乞舌兒吉速惕-突︀舌兒 Kirgisud-tur

sentences.l: Jüči Oirat, Buriyat, Barγun, Ursud, Qabqanas, Qaṅγas, Tubas-(object) having-made-enter, ten-thousand Kirghiz-to arriving-when,
sentences.i: When Jüchi had brought in the Oirat, Buriyat, Barqun, Ursut, Qabqanas, Qangqas and Tubas, and reached the ten thousand of the Kirghiz,
sentences.n: A list of peoples (Ming 種(名) each), the accusative -i falling on the last, Tubas-i, for them all. oroγ̇uluγ̇ad is 'having made enter' (causative -γ̇ul- + converb -γ̇ad). kürüġesü is kürü- 'to reach' with the conditional converb -ġesü (Ming 到呵), 'when he reached'. tümen Kirgisud-tur is 'to the ten-thousand of the Kirghiz' (Ming 萬 種(名)行). Doubtful: the names. Qaṅγas has the Ming 破開的 'split open' in an earlier part; here the Ming gives only 種(名), and I take it as a people.

sentences.i: the lords of the Kirghiz, Jedi, Inal, Aldiger and Örebek Digin, submitted,
sentences.n: nojad is nojan 'lord' with the plural -d (Ming 官人每). The four names have the Ming 人名 (Jedi, Inal, Aldiger with (人)名). The list is apposed to Kirgisud-un nojad, which is repeated before the verbs elsen orožu, 'entered in submission'. Digin is probably a title (as in 'prince'), but the Ming gives 人名 and I keep it with the name: Örebek-Digin.

sentences.l: White-ones gyrfalcons, white-ones geldings, black-ones sables taking, coming, Jüči-to had-an-audience.
sentences.i: They came with white gyrfalcons, white geldings and black sables, and paid their respects to Jüchi.
sentences.n: Three pairs of epithet and noun: čaγaγ̇a-nuγ̇ud šiṅqod, čaγaγ̇a-nuγ̇ud aγtas, qara-nuγ̇ud buluγad. The Ming glosses each word separately (白每 海靑每, 白每 騸馬每, 黑每 貂鼠每). -nuγ̇ud is a plural (Ming 每) that turns 'white' and 'black' into 'white ones', 'black ones'. The nouns are plural too: šiṅqod from šiṅqor 'gyrfalcon' (stem inferred from the Ming 海靑), aγtas from aγta 'gelding' (plural -s), buluγad from buluγan 'sable'. Doubtful: whether the white ones go with the falcons and the geldings both, as I have it, and whether čaγaγ̇a is čaγaγan 'white' (the stem as printed is shorter). The chain ends aγ̇ulžaba 'had an audience' with Žüči-de (dative -de).

sentences.i: Jüchi, in this way, brought in the Forest People, from the Shibir, Kesdiin, Baid, Tuqas, Tenlek, Tögeles, Tas, and the Bajigid on,
sentences.n: A list of peoples again, then 'from the Bažigid' (-d plural + -āča ablative, Ming 處), written across a line-end by Shiratori: Bažigi- on one line, d-āča on the next. inaγši is 'thus, in this way' (Ming 以這相). hoi-jin irgen-i is 'the forest people' (Ming 林的百姓行) with the accusative -i, the object of oroγ̇ulžu 'making enter' (Ming 敎投入着). Doubtful: the sense of '…from the Bajigid on', which I take as 'beginning with the first-named and going on to the last, so many peoples'; the Ming 處 is 'at/from'.

sentences.t: Kirgisud-un tümed-ün miṅγad-un nojad-i hoi-jin irgen-ü nojad-i abuγ̇ad irežü

sentences.l: Kirghiz-of ten-thousands-of thousands-of lords-(object), forest-of people-of lords-(object) taking, coming,
sentences.i: he took the lords of the Kirghiz tümens and thousands, and the lords of the Forest People, and came,
sentences.n: Kirgisud-un tümed-ün miṅγad-un nojad-i is three genitives in a row, 'of the Kirghiz, of the ten-thousands, of the thousands, the lords': tümed-ün (tümen + plural -d + -ün) and miṅγad-un (miṅγan + -d + -un, Ming 千每的 'of the thousands'). nojad-i takes the accusative. hoi-jin irgen-ü nojad-i is 'the lords of the forest people'. abuγ̇ad irežü is 'taking, coming' (Ming 將來了, 來着). The Mongol does not say who 'took' them; I take Jüchi.

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan-to white-ones gyrfalcons-with, white-ones geldings-with, black-ones sables-with made-to-have-an-audience.
sentences.i: He presented them to Chinggis Qahan, together with the white gyrfalcons, the white geldings and the black sables.
sentences.n: Three instrumentals in -(i)jar: siṅqod(i)-jar, aγtas(i)-jar, buluγad(i)-jar, each with Shiratori's linking (i) (Ming 敎 'causing, by means of'). The verb aγ̇ulžaγ̇ulba is the causative (-γ̇ul-) of aγ̇ulža- 'to have an audience', 'had them received, presented them'. Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur has the dative -dur. The sense is that Jüchi had the Kirghiz lords presented, 'with' the animals.

words.reading: 中忽都︀中合-別乞-冝 Quduqa-Beki-ji

morph.gloss: Quduqa Beki, a man's name [人名行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to meet, welcome (stem inferred from the Ming 迎接; uncertain) [迎接]
to submit (stem inferred from the Ming 投降/歸附) [歸附]

sentences.l: Oirat-of Quduqa-Beki-(object) "welcoming, formerly submitting, ten-thousand Oirat-own leading came saying, favouring,
sentences.i: Saying, “Quduqa Beki of the Oirat came to meet us, having earlier submitted, and brought his own ten thousand Oirat,” [Chinggis] showed him favour,
sentences.n: A tangle of case. Quduqa-Beki-ji takes the accusative -ji and is the object of sojurγažu 'favouring' at the end; the words between are quoted. Shiratori prints an opening mark before uγtun but no closing mark; I close it in `i` after irebe, where keġen 'saying' follows. Doubtful: uγtun (Ming 迎接 'to meet, welcome') I take as a converb of a stem uγtu-, which I know only from the Ming. urida elsen is 'formerly submitting'; Oirad(i)-jan has the reflexive -jan 'own'; uduridun is a converb in -dun (Ming 引着), 'leading'. In `i` the opening mark is moved back to Quduqa Beki's name so that the plain line runs in English order (he is also the object of 'showed him favour'); `l` keeps Shiratori's placement. The subject of sojurγažu is not written; [Chinggis] in `i` is supplied.

sentences.i: He gave Checheigen to Inalchi, Quduqa Beki's son.
sentences.n: köġün-e is 'to the son' (dative-locative -e, Ming 兒子行), in-ü 'his' (the third-person genitive, placed after its noun; Quduqa Beki's), Inalči-da 'to Inalchi' (-da after a vowel). Čečeigen-i is the accusative (Ming 女子名). The Ming says nothing of whose son; it is Quduqa Beki's, by the sentence before.

sentences.i: To Törelchi, Inalchi's elder brother, he gave Qoluiqan, Jüchi's daughter.
sentences.n: Inalči-jin aqa is 'Inalchi's elder brother' (genitive -jin after a vowel; Ming 的 兄), Törelči-de the dative. Žuči-jin öki is 'Jüchi's daughter' (Ming 子名的 女子), and Qoluiγan-i the accusative of the woman given (Ming 女名行). The Mongol names no giver; the gifts follow from the Qahan's favour just granted, and the unit before has the Qahan favouring Quduqa Beki, so the 'he' of the plain line is probably the Qahan; the Mongol does not say, and I leave it unstated.

sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan showed favour to Jüchi and said:
sentences.n: Čiṅgis Qaγan is the subject, Žüči-ji the object (-ji), sojurγažu 'showing favour' a converb, and ügülerün 'when saying' (-rün) introduces the speech with Shiratori's colon. The speech's opening mark is on the next word and its closing mark on ögsü" at the end of the section's last speech.

sentences.t: "Köġüd-ün min-u aqa či.

morph.gloss: my, of me (bi, genitive stem min-, + -u, set after its noun) [我的]

sentences.l: "Sons-of my eldest you.
sentences.i: “Of my sons, you are the eldest.
sentences.n: Köġüd-ün is köġün 'son' with the plural -d and the genitive -ün: 'of the sons' (Ming 兒子的). min-u 'my' and aqa 'elder brother' (Ming 長 'eldest', the noun used as an adjective); či 'you'. The Mongol has no copula. The opening mark on "Köġüd-ün is Shiratori's; the speech runs to ögsü" three units on.

sentences.t: Ger-tēče sai γarču mör saitu oduγsan γažar-a

morph.gloss: just, only now (Ming 纔; the usual meaning of sai is 'good') [纔]

sentences.l: Home-from just going-out, track good-having gone land-to,
sentences.i: Setting out from home, you went by a good road into lands,
sentences.n: ger-tēče is 'from home' (ablative -tēče, the long-vowel spelling of -teče; Ming 從家裏); γarču 'going out' (γar-, converb -ču, Ming 出着). sai is read 'just' (Ming 纔) rather than 'good'; saitu is sai + the possessive -tu, 'having good' (Ming 好有的), and mör 'road' (Ming 道子), so 'good-tracked' and 'by a good road'. oduγsan is the past participle of od- 'to go' (Ming 去了的), γažar-a 'to the land' (Ming 地面行). Doubtful: the clause is a relative: 'the land that you went to', and the next unit takes up what happened there.

sentences.t: ere aγta-ji ülü širqan ülü žobaγ̇an ölžeitü hoi-jin irgen-i oroγ̇ulžu irebe či.

sentences.l: Man gelding-(object) not harming, not troubling, blessed, forest-of people-(object) making-enter came you.
sentences.i: Without harming man or horse, without hardship, and blessed with good fortune, you came, having brought the Forest People in.
sentences.n: ülü 'not' stands before two converbs, širqan and žobaγ̇an (-n, Ming 傷着 'harming', 生受着 'suffering'); the stems širqa- and žobaγ̇a- are inferred from the Ming. ölžeitü is ölžei 'good fortune' + the possessive -tü (Ming 福有的). aγta-ji is the accusative of 'gelding, horse'. Doubtful: ere aγta-ji ülü širqan, which could also be read 'man, not harming the horse'; the Ming has 人 馬行 不傷着. The chain ends oroγ̇ulžu irebe či 'having brought in, came, you', with či at the end for the sentence's person.

sentences.l: People to-you I-give" saying, decree made.
sentences.i: I give you the people,” he said. So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: Irge is a form of irgen 'people' (Ming 百姓), čima-da the dative of či 'you' on the oblique stem (Ming 你行). ögsü is the optative 'I will give', and Shiratori's closing mark stands on it. keġen žarliγ bolba: 'saying, a decree became' (bolba, Ming 做了); žarliγ is the Ming's 聖旨 'imperial decree'. Both of Shiratori's marks on this speech are printed: the opening on "Köġüd-ün (U28), the closing here.

sentences.n: Basa 'again' (Ming 再). Boroγ̇ul nojan-i is 'Boroqul the noyan' with the accusative -i (Ming 官人行). Qori-Tumad is a people (Ming 種(名)), with irgen-dür 'to the people' (Ming 百姓行). čaγ̇uraγ̇ulba is čaγ̇ura- 'to go out on campaign' (stem from the Ming 出征) with the causative -γ̇ul- and -ba: 'sent out on campaign'.

sentences.i: When Daiduqul-Soqos, the noyan of the Tumad people, died, his wife Botoqui-Tarqun was in charge of the Tumad people.
sentences.n: Tumad irgen-ü nojan is 'noyan of the Tumad people' (irgen-ü, genitive after n). üküġesü is ükü- 'to die' with the conditional converb -ġesü (Ming 死了呵), 'when he died'. eme in-ü is 'wife his' (Ming 妻 他的). medežü is mede- 'to know' (here 'to manage', Ming 管着 'have charge of') and ažuγ̇u the narrative past 'was' (Ming 有來), so 'was managing'. Doubtful: medežü ažuγ̇u as 'was in charge'; the same word in the previous parts is 'knowing' (Ming 知着).

sentences.t: Boroγul nojan kürčü γurban haran jeke čerig-eče urida jabura odču
sentences.l: Boroγul noyan arriving, three people great army-from ahead going, going,
sentences.i: Boroqul the noyan, with three men, went on ahead of the great army,
sentences.n: Boroγul nojan kürčü 'Boroqul the noyan, arriving' (kür-, converb -čü after r, Ming 到着). γurban haran is 'three people' (Ming 三 人). jeke čerig-eče is 'from the great army' (ablative -eče, Ming 軍處), urida 'in front, ahead'. jabura odču is 'going, going' (Ming 行 去着): jabu- 'to walk, go' with -ra, which I take as a converb, and od- with -ču. Doubtful: jabura (Ming 行 alone); I take the pair as one idea, 'going ahead'. kürčü 'arriving' is not carried into the plain line, which gives only the going ahead.

sentences.n: qaraγ̇ul-a is 'scout' with the dative-locative -a in the sense 'by' (Ming 哨望的行): the scouts are the doers, and the Ming 行 marks them as agents. an-u is 'their' (the third-person genitive after its noun), qoinaγ̇un 'behind' (Ming 自後 'from behind'). dermedtežü, boγ̇ožu and barižu are converbs (Ming 劫據着, 阻着, 拿着); dermedte- and boγ̇o- are inferred from the Ming. alažuγ̇ui is ala- 'to kill' with the past -žuγ̇ui (Ming 殺了有). sentences.n: Boγ̇orču and Muqali are names (Ming 人名), with qojar 'two' after them (Ming 兩箇). Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-i has the accusative. baitala is 'right up to, until' (Ming 止住直到 'stopping, until'), perhaps bai- 'to stand' with -tala; here it carries the sense 'stop'. idγaba is idγa- 'to urge' (stem inferred from the Ming 勸) with the past -ba. Doubtful: the whole clause, 'persuaded the Qahan to stop'; the Ming has 止住直到 and 勸了.

morph.gloss: the Dörbetei, a clan or surname (Ming 姓名) [姓(名)]

words.reading: 朶舌兒伯-多黑失泥 Dorbai-Doγšin-i

morph.gloss: Dorbai Doqshin, a man's name [人名行]

sentences.l: But Dörbetei Dorbai-Doγšin-(object) appointing-when,
sentences.i: But when he appointed Dorbai Doqshin of the Dörbetei,
sentences.n: žiči 'but' (Ming 郤). Dörbetei is a clan or surname (Ming 姓(名)); Dorbai-Doγšin-i takes the accusative (Ming 人名行). tüširün is tüši- 'to appoint, entrust' (Ming 委付) with the converb of time -rün. Doubtful: whether Dörbetei names the clan or is a title of the man; I keep it as a clan before the name.

sentences.t: čerig qataṅγuj-a žasažu müṅke teṅgeri-ji žalbarižu Tumad irgen-i oroγ̇ulun sori keġen žarliγ bolba.

morph.gloss: hard, stern (Ming 嚴; form uncertain) [嚴行]
to prepare, set in order [整治着]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
people, the common folk [百姓 行]

sentences.l: Army sternly arranging, Eternal Heaven-(object) praying, Tumad people-(object) making-enter, try saying decree became.
sentences.i: “Arrange the army sternly, pray to Eternal Heaven, and try to bring the Tumad people in,” he said; so it was decreed.
sentences.n: A chain of converbs: žasažu 'arranging' (Ming 整治着), žalbarižu 'praying' (Ming 禱吿着), then oroγ̇ulun 'making enter' (Ming 敎入) and sori 'try' (Ming 試). qataṅγuj-a is the dative-locative -a used as an adverb (Ming 嚴 行), 'with sternness'. Müṅke teṅgeri-ji is 'Eternal Heaven' (müṅke 'eternal', Ming 長生 'long life') with the accusative -ji. keġen žarliγ bolba: 'saying, a decree became'. Shiratori prints no quotation marks here; I supply them in `i` only. Doubtful: the sense of oroγ̇ulun sori, 'make them enter, try'.

sentences.t: Dorbai čerig žasarun urida čerig-ün jabuqu Qaraγ̇ul-un sakiqu mör horum sübes-tür hoγtorγou erbegežeġülžü

morph.gloss: to arrange, put in order [整治時]
genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant)
genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant)
gap, pass, opening (Ming 口子) [口子每 裏]

words.reading: 額舌兒別格折兀勒周 erbegežeġülžü

morph.gloss: to make a show, put on a display (Ming 張形勢; stem uncertain) [張形勢着]

sentences.l: Dorbai, army arranging-when, ahead army-of going scouts-of guarding road by-path pass-in empty making-a-show,
sentences.i: Dorbai, as he arranged the army, made a false show of emptiness at the passes on the roads and by-paths ahead, where the army moves and the scouts keep guard,
sentences.n: A long chain. žasarun is the converb of time (-run, Ming 整治時 'when arranging'). čerig-ün jabuqu and Qaraγ̇ul-un sakiqu are two participles in -qu (Ming 行的, 守的) with the genitive: 'the going of the army', 'the guarding of the scouts'. mör horum is 'road, by-path' (Ming 路 逕), sübes-tür 'at the passes' (sübe 'gap, mouth', Ming 口子每裏; the plural -s and -tür). hoγtorγou erbegežeġülžü: 'empty' (Ming 虛) and 'making a show' (Ming 張形勢着; erbege-, an extension -že- of unclear force and the causative -ġül- are inferred and doubtful). Doubtful: the sense of the whole, 'a false show of emptiness' (a feint), is the Ming's 虛張形勢.

sentences.t: hulaγ̇an buqa-jin jabuγsan mör(i)-jer čeriġüd-tür žasaγlarun

words.reading: 忽剌安 不中合-因 hulaγ̇an buqa-jin
扯舌里兀惕-突︀舌兒 čeriġüd-tür

morph.gloss: to give orders, proclaim (stem inferred from the Ming 傳號令) [傳號令時]

sentences.l: Red bull-of gone track-along, troops-to giving-orders-when,
sentences.i: and, as he gave orders to the troops, along the track the red bull had trodden,
sentences.n: hulaγ̇an buqa-jin: 'of the red bull' (Ming 獸名的 'beast's name'; -jin after a vowel). jabuγsan mör(i)-jer is 'the track gone' (past participle jabuγsan, Ming 行了的) 'along' (-(i)jer with Shiratori's linking (i), Ming 依着). čeriġüd-tür is 'to the troops' (Ming 軍每行) and žasaγlarun 'when giving orders' (Ming 傳號令時; stem žasaγla- inferred). Doubtful: the red bull, which I take as a wild animal whose track the army follows; the Ming gives only 獸名, and buqa could be 'bull' or 'stag'.

sentences.t: čerig-ün toγ̇otu küġün žirüge jadaγ̇asu mišiquj-a ere-dür harban müsüd ürgeġülžü

morph.gloss: genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant)
to be unable (Ming 不能) [不能呵]
to strike, fight (Shiratori prints mišiquj-a; the transcription 你 and the glossary read niši-) [打的行]
rod, stick, arrow shaft (Ming 條子) [條子(每)]
to carry on the back (stem inferred from the Ming 背) [敎背着]

sentences.l: Army-of counted man heart if-unable, to-the-striking man ten rods making-carry,
sentences.i: for the army's counted men, if their heart failed, he made the men who fight carry ten rods each,
sentences.n: čerig-ün toγ̇otu küġün: 'a man of the army's count' (toγ̇otu, Ming 正數有的, is toγ̇o 'count' + -tu 'having'). žirüge 'heart' and jadaγ̇asu 'if (they) cannot' (Ming 不能呵). mišiquj-a is printed with m but the transcription has 你 (ni): it is read niši-, 'to strike', with the participle -quj before the vowel of -a, 'to those who strike' (Ming 打的行). harban müsüd is 'ten rods' (müsü, Ming 條子, with plural -d); ürgeġülžü is 'making carry' (ürge- inferred from the Ming 背, with the causative -ġül-). Doubtful: the whole unit. I cannot tell how 'if the heart cannot' joins the ten rods, nor who bears them; the literal line follows the Ming word by word and the plain line is a guess.

sentences.t: süke uγali kirüġe šiγ̇uči ere-jin žer žebseg žasaγ̇ulžu

words.reading: 折舌兒 折卜薛克 žer žebseg

morph.gloss: tool (the Ming 器械 is shared with žebseg) [器︀械]
to prepare, set in order [敎整治着]

sentences.l: Axe, adze, saw, chisel, man-of tools, weapons having-prepared,
sentences.i: and had axes, adzes, saws and chisels, the men's tools and weapons, got ready,
sentences.n: A list of four tools (Ming 斧子, 錛子, 鋸子, 鑿子), then ere-jin žer žebseg: 'the man's tools' (ere-jin, genitive after a vowel; Ming 男子的) and žer žebseg (the Ming gives both 器械 'arms, equipment'). žasaγ̇ulžu is žasa- 'to prepare' with the causative -γ̇ul- and the converb -žu (Ming 敎整治着). uγali 'adze' is a guess from the Ming 錛子.

sentences.t: hulaγ̇an buqa-jin jabuγsan mör(i)-jer mör-tür baiγsan modud hoγtočin čabčiγ̇ulžu kirügedeġülžü mör bolγažu

words.reading: 忽剌安 不中合-因 hulaγ̇an buqa-jin

morph.gloss: to cut off (stem inferred from the Ming 斷) [斷着]
to chop, hew (stem inferred from the Ming 斫) [斫着]

words.reading: 乞舌魯格迭兀勒周 kirügedeġülžü

sentences.l: Red bull-of gone track-along, road-on standing trees cutting-off, chopping, having-had-sawn, road making,
sentences.i: and along the red bull's track they cut down the trees that stood on the road, chopped and sawed them, and made a road,
sentences.n: The same phrase as before: hulaγ̇an buqa-jin jabuγsan mör(i)-jer. mör-tür baiγsan modud is 'the trees (mod, plural -d) that stood on the road' (baiγsan, Ming 立的, a participle of bai- 'to stand'; mör-tür Ming 路行). The chain: hoγtočin (Ming 斷着 'cutting off'), čabčiγ̇ulžu (Ming 斫着 'chopping'), kirügedeġülžü (Ming 敎鋸着 'having (them) sawn', from kirüġe 'saw'), mör bolγažu (Ming 敎做着 'making a road'). Doubtful: the stems hoγto- and čabči- and the shapes of the endings (-čin, -ġül-), all inferred from the Ming.

sentences.t: aγ̇ula deġere γaruγ̇asu Tumad irgen-ü erüge deġerēče gened qurimlan saγ̇uqui-dur daγ̇uliba.

morph.gloss: to go out, go up [上呵]
smoke-hole, roof-window of a tent (Ming 天窗) [天窻]

sentences.l: Mountain above going-up-when, Tumad people-of smoke-hole above-from unawares feasting sitting-when plundered.
sentences.i: When they climbed the mountain, they fell unawares, from above their smoke-hole, on the Tumad people sitting at a feast, and plundered them.
sentences.n: aγ̇ula deġere γaruγ̇asu: 'on the mountain, when they went up' (γar- 'to go up, go out', Ming 上呵). erüge deġerēče is 'from above the smoke-hole' (erüge, the roof-window of a tent, Ming 天窗; deġerēče, ablative with the long-vowel spelling), i.e. looking in from the top of the tent. gened 'suddenly, unawares' (Ming 不意). qurimlan saγ̇uqui-dur is 'feasting' (qurim 'feast' + -la- + -n, Ming 做筵 'making a feast') 'when sitting' (saγ̇u- + -qui + -dur, Ming 坐的時). daγ̇uliba 'plundered' (Ming 據了 'seized'). Doubtful: the 'smoke-hole': the Ming 上處 'above' might mean the upper end of the camp; I keep the literal 'from above the smoke-hole'.

sentences.t: Urida Qorči nojan, Quduγa-Beki qojar Tumad-ta bariγdažu Botoqui-Tarqun-dur tende ažuγ̇u.

morph.gloss: Quduqa Beki, a man's name (printed with γ beside Quduqa-Beki) [人名]
two (follows the pair it counts) [兩箇]
dative-locative: by (agent of a passive; after d)

words.reading: 孛脫中灰-塔舌兒中渾-突︀舌兒 Botoqui-Tarqun-dur

glyphs.s: 孛脫中灰-塔舌兒中渾-突︀舌兒

morph.gloss: Botoqui-Tarqun, a woman's name [婦人名行]
past narrative (back-vowel form; Ming 有來)

sentences.l: Formerly Qorči noyan, Quduγa-Beki two Tumad-by being-seized, Botoqui-Tarqun-at there were.
sentences.i: Earlier, Qorchi the noyan and Quduqa Beki had been seized by the Tumad, and were there at Botoqui-Tarqun's.
sentences.n: Urida 'formerly'; Qorči nojan 'Qorchi the noyan'; Quduγa-Beki with γ (the Ming has the same characters as Quduqa); qojar 'two'. Tumad-ta has the dative-locative -ta after d in the sense 'by' (Ming 行), the agent of the passive bariγdažu (bari- 'to seize' + the passive -γda- + the converb -žu, Ming 被拿着). Botoqui-Tarqun-dur is 'at Botoqui-Tarqun's (place)' (-dur, Ming 行), tende 'there', ažuγ̇u 'was' (Ming 有來). Doubtful: the Ming has no 'with'; I read the dative as 'at her place'.

sentences.t: Qorči-jin bariγdaqu josun Tumad irgen-ü ökid γoγ̇astan γučin emes abtuγai keġen žarliγ boluγsan-dur

morph.gloss: Qorchi, a man's name [人名 的]
custom, reason, the right way (Ming 道理) [道理]
beautiful (stem inferred from the Ming 美) [美每有(的每)]

sentences.l: Qorči-of being-seized reason, Tumad people-of girls beautiful thirty wives let-him-take saying decree become-when,
sentences.i: When it was decreed, “By right of Qorchi’s capture, let him take thirty of the fair girls of the Tumad people as wives,”
sentences.n: Qorči-jin bariγdaqu josun: 'Qorchi's being seized, the reason' (bariγdaqu is the participle of the passive, Ming 被拿的; josun 'right, reason', Ming 道理). Tumad irgen-ü ökid γoγ̇astan is 'the Tumad people's girls, the fair ones' (ökid, plural of ökin; γoγ̇astan, Ming 美每有(的每), with an ending I read as a collective -tan), γučin emes abtuγai: 'thirty wives let (him) take' (emes, plural of eme; abtuγai, the third-person optative, Ming 受者). keġen žarliγ boluγsan-dur is 'saying, when the decree had become' (-dur on the participle, Ming 時). Shiratori has no quotation marks here; I supply them in `i`. Doubtful: γoγ̇astan; the stem is read from the Ming alone.

sentences.t: Tumad irgen-ü ökid abqu keġen odqu bolun
sentences.l: Tumad people-of girls to-take saying going being-when,
sentences.i: and as he was about to go and take the Tumad people's girls,
sentences.n: abqu is the participle of ab- 'to take' (Ming 要), odqu the participle of od- 'to go' (Ming 去的), then bolun 'being, when' (Ming 做). The pair means 'about to go'. keġen 'saying' marks the girls as the thing named in the decree.

sentences.t: urida elsegsed irgen žiči bulγa bolžu Qorči nojan-i barižuγ̇ui.

morph.gloss: past participle, plural: those who had …ed

sentences.l: Formerly submitted people but rebelling, Qorči noyan-(object) had-seized.
sentences.i: the people who had earlier submitted rebelled and seized Qorchi the noyan.
sentences.n: urida 'formerly'; elsegsed 'those who had submitted' (else- 'to submit', past participle plural -gsed, Ming 投降了的每); irgen 'people'; žiči 'but' (Ming 郤). bulγa bolžu is 'becoming rebellion', i.e. rebelling (Ming 反 做着). Qorči nojan-i has the accusative; barižuγ̇ui is bari- 'to seize' with the past -žuγ̇ui (Ming 拿了有來).

sentences.t: Qorči Tumad-ta bariγda- žuγ̇u keġen Čiṅgis Qaγan medežü

morph.gloss: dative-locative: by (agent of a passive; after d)
past narrative (second half of bariγda-žuγ̇u; Ming 有) [有]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]
to know, to manage (Ming 管着 'have charge of'; 知着 'knowing') [知着]

sentences.l: Qorči Tumad-by had-been-seized saying, Chinggis Qaγan knowing,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan learned that “Qorchi has been seized by the Tumad,”
sentences.n: bariγda- is split by Shiratori's hyphen from -žuγ̇u on the next word (Ming 被拿了 + 有): bari- + the passive -γda- + -žuγ̇u, 'has been seized'. Tumad-ta has -ta in the sense 'by'. keġen 'saying' then medežü 'knowing' (Ming 麽道, 知着), so 'knowing that …'. The quotation marks are mine, in `i` only.

sentences.t: hoi-in irgen-ü jabudal Quduqa medemü-že keġežü ileġesü
sentences.l: Forest-of people-of going-about Quduqa knows-indeed saying, if-he-sent,
sentences.i: and, saying, “Quduqa knows the ways of the Forest People,” he sent him.
sentences.n: hoi-in irgen-ü jabudal: 'the forest people's going about' (hoi-in, genitive; jabudal from jabu- 'to go', tentative, Ming 行 'conduct, movements'). Quduqa medemü-že: 'Quduqa knows indeed' (medemü, present of mede-; -že an assertion particle, Ming 也者). keġežü 'saying' and ileġesü 'if (he) sends' (Ming 敎去呵). Doubtful: ileġesü, read 'when he sent (him)'; the Ming is the conditional 呵. jabudal is read tentatively as 'movements, doings' from the Ming 行動. Shiratori prints no quotation marks here; I supply them in `i`.

sentences.t: Quduγa-Beki Basa bariγdažuγ̇u. Tumad irgen-i oroγ̇ulun baraγ̇asu

morph.gloss: Quduqa Beki, a man's name (printed with γ beside Quduqa-Beki) [人名]
people, the common folk [百姓 行]
to end, be finished (here an auxiliary: when done) [了呵]

sentences.l: Quduγa-Beki again was-seized, Tumad people-(object) making-enter finished-when,
sentences.i: Quduqa Beki was seized again; and when the Tumad people had been brought in,
sentences.n: Quduγa-Beki Basa bariγdažuγ̇u: 'Quduqa Beki again was seized' (basa 'again', Ming 再; bariγdažuγ̇u is bari- + the passive -γda- + the narrative past -žuγ̇u, Ming 被拿了有). Tumad irgen-i oroγ̇ulun baraγ̇asu: 'the Tumad people making enter, finished-if' (baraγ̇asu, Ming 了呵, bara- 'to end' as an auxiliary, 'when done'). The subject of the bringing-in is not named.

sentences.t: Boroγul-un jasun-u tula žaγ̇un Tumad-i ögbe.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant)
because of, on account of (Ming 上頭) [上頭]

sentences.l: Boroγul-of bone-of on-account hundred Tumad-(object) gave.
sentences.i: he gave a hundred of the Tumad on account of Boroqul’s bones.
sentences.n: Boroγul-un jasun-u tula: 'Boroqul's bones, on account of' (Ming 骨頭的上頭; tula 'because of', Ming 上頭, 'on top of', hence 'for that reason'). žaγ̇un Tumad-i: 'a hundred Tumad' (Ming 百) with the accusative -i. Doubtful: 'on account of the bones' is the Ming's own, a gift made in compensation for the dead man's remains; I do not say 'blood-price' since the text does not.

sentences.t: Qorči γučin ökid-i abuba.
sentences.l: Qorči thirty girls-(object) took.
sentences.i: Qorchi took the thirty girls.
sentences.n: Qorči γučin ökid-i abuba: 'Qorchi thirty girls took'. ökid-i is the plural ökid with the accusative -i (Ming 女子(每)行); abuba is ab- 'to take' with the past -uba (Ming 要了, with a linking u).

sentences.t: Quduqa-Beki-de Botoqui-Tarqun-i ögbe.

sentences.l: Quduqa-Beki-to Botoqui-Tarqun-(object) gave.
sentences.i: To Quduqa Beki he gave Botoqui-Tarqun.
sentences.n: Quduqa-Beki-de is the dative -de (Ming 人名行), Botoqui-Tarqun-i the accusative (Ming 婦人名行), and ögbe the past 'gave'. The woman is the one in whose camp the two men had been held at the beginning of the section.
